The Federal Government has pledged to intervene in compensation disputes affecting residents impacted by railway construction in Zaria, Kaduna State, while considering a request to name a proposed railway extension after the grandfather of the Emir of Zazzau. The Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Funso Adebiyi, gave the assurances in a statement on Friday following a courtesy visit to the palace of the Emir of Zazzau, Ahmad Bamali, as part of efforts to strengthen engagement with traditional institutions and host communities on railway development. Adebiyi disclosed that the ministry would review the request to name the proposed railway extension in recognition of the historical contributions of the Emir’s grandfather to the establishment of railway transportation in Zaria. He also pledged to personally intervene in the compensation issues affecting residents whose properties and interests had been impacted by the railway construction project. According to the statement, he assured the monarch that the ministry would “examine the complaints and work towards an acceptable resolution.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Adebiyi acknowledged concerns arising from the existing statutory framework governing compensation, saying the ministry would “undertake the necessary review to address the grievances of affected residents.” He further disclosed that he planned to meet with the affected residents the following week to examine their complaints, review relevant records and determine appropriate steps towards resolving the outstanding issues. Pastors’ heavenly tales spark earthly row 2027: APC scribe urges support for Tinubu Tinubu has fulfilled promises to Kaduna, says Uba Sani The permanent secretary also assured the Emir that the ministry would “give the matter the required attention” and work to ensure that the compensation concerns were addressed as promptly as possible. He thanked the monarch for receiving the delegation and commended his hospitality, noting that “sustained collaboration with traditional institutions was essential to the successful implementation of railway infrastructure projects.” Earlier, Bamali had expressed delight at the return of railway services to Zaria, describing the development as “a significant milestone that rekindled the historical relationship between rail transportation and the Zazzau Emirate.” Recalling his childhood experience with the railway, the monarch said he travelled from Zaria to Bauchi in 1949 to see a train for the first time. He described the experience as “a memorable part of the area’s railway history.” The Emir stressed that railway development in Zaria had historical roots that deserved greater recognition, particularly the contributions of individuals who initiated and facilitated the project. He consequently appealed to the Federal Government to consider naming the proposed railway extension after his grandfather in recognition of his role in railway establishment in Kaduna State. Bamali urged the permanent secretary to convey the request to the Minister of Transportation and President Bola Tinubu, expressing hope that the government would give it favourable consideration.
